newsitem.title: INDIA: Malaysia PM Mahathir upbeat on India's ASEAN links.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM Mahathir upbeat on India's ASEAN links.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Saturday prospects were good for improving ecomomic ties between India and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).

"I wish to reiterate here that there are indeed good prospects for improving economic and business opportunities between ASEAN and India," Mahathir said in an inaugural speech at an India-ASEAN lecture series.

He said prime sectors for the development of ties between ASEAN and India were oil and natural gas, agriculture and agro-based technology, biotechnology, power and telcommunications, information technology, railways and roads, civil aviation and financial services.
He encouraged Indian investment participation in the ASEAN-Mekong Basin Development Cooperation project and other sub-regional growth areas.
He also invited Indian information technology companies to invest in Malaysia's Multi-Media Super Corridor Project.
He said dialogue with ASEAN would help raise awareness of India's efforts to liberalise and end old perceptions of an over-bureaucratic and closed economy.

Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand have led ASEAN's investment and trade drive in India, while Indonesia and the Philippines have joined in too. ASEAN investment in India was $372 million in 1995, while trade totalled $4.6 billion.

At the start of a three-day official visit to India on Friday, Nahathir had poured cold water on Indian hopes of a quick entry into the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, saying the grouping would become unwieldy if more nations were to join.
APEC includes 18 countries from Asia, North America and South America which hope to achieve free regional trade by 2020.
India has been seeking membership of APEC, which currently has a moratorium on new members.

India was given full dialogue status with ASEAN in July. ASEAN groups Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam. Burma, Cambodia and Laos are expected to join next year.
